functions.plate_comment: RRSLAM v2 stream writer. 0x1abc0-0x1abde writes 10-byte RRSLAM/version=2/header-length=20 prefix; 0x1ac00-0x1ac78 writes five LE words: scale=20,left,top,width,height. GridDiskHeaderV2 is byte-aligned disk documentation ONLY, never an in-memory grid cast. Extracts active view from metadata+0x10 into row-major byte buffer; initializes to 0x80, copies rows using full bounds stride. Product is low 32 bits of width*height; width loop is signed >0, row limit unsigned. 0x1ad0a-0x1ad38 writes cells then 16-byte MD5 of cells only. Skips later stages on stream state bit 1 (badbit), not failbit. Does not rename, fsync, or select a filename. Returns stream pointer; does not establish durability. Zero product uses NULL buffer and helper emits zero digest, not MD5(empty). Occupancy probability mapping unresolved.

functions.signature: GridBufferRef *GridGetBuffer(GridBufferRef *out, void *store, const int *index, const unsigned char *fill)
functions.plate_comment: Gets/creates pointer-table slot indexed directly by *index, NOT a native flag. Existing cells return valid=1 immediately. Missing slot: 1024x1024 allocation (0x100000 bytes), centered bounds via 0x21dc0, fill every cell from *fill, metadata stride36. Allocation failure sets only out->valid=0; other result fields are not established. No lock in this routine. ABI-level explicit result pointer, not invented original C++ return signature.
functions.name: GridGetBuffer

functions.plate_comment: V2 body; dispatcher has already consumed 10 bytes. Reads 20-byte view block: scale,left,top,width,height. Requires scale==20 at 0x1d29c; computes low-32-bit width*height at 0x1d2ba with no explicit dimension/bounds/overflow validation. Reads byte cells and 16-byte digest. All four words must compare at 0x1d324/0x1d33e/0x1d346/0x1d34e before mutation. Digest excludes entire header. Success resets full existing target to 0x80, merges file rectangle into active view, copies rows using target bounds and stride. Width copy condition signed >0; height iteration unsigned. Scale or MD5 rejection returns same stream without explicit setstate; outer stream-state success does NOT prove cells accepted. Intermediate checks test only state bit 1 (badbit), not failbit. No trailing-length or occupancy-value validation. No lock in this function; caller synchronization unresolved.
functions.name: GridReadV2

functions.plate_comment: Reads 10-byte prefix. Magic checks 0x1d488-0x1d4a6 compare RRSLAM (0x4c535252,0x4d41). Matching magic: version 2 requires uint16 header-length 20 then GridReadV2; version 1 requires 36 then legacy 0x1cf60. Unknown version/header length returns without setstate. Magic mismatch calls legacy 0x1ca54 after prefix read; legacy seek/format behavior not recovered here. Returns stream pointer, not format-validation status. Tests bit 1 only internally.

functions.plate_comment: Storage cache loader: index=*flag+11. Existing pointer bypasses file read, returns GridGetBuffer result. Otherwise obtains 1024x1024 buffer filled 0x80, copies GridFilenameSlot string and opens input mode 8. Calls GridReadDispatch, accepts if stream state &5 ==0. On allocation/open/stream failure drops same cache slot with base11 and sets out->valid=0. Header/scale/digest mismatch need not set stream state: can return valid=1 with initialized unchanged cells and retain cache. No lock around cache lookup/load/drop observed; dmb/ldrex/strex belong to string reference count, not cache synchronization. Close result is ignored. ABI explicit out pointer; original C++ class/layout unknown.

functions.signature: void GridCellDigest(const unsigned char *cells, unsigned int length, unsigned char *digest)
functions.plate_comment: 16-byte MD5-compatible helper for ordinary grids (<2^29 bytes): standard IV at0x3f434, 64-byte blocks, 0x80 padding and four output words. Bit-length low word is length<<3 and high word is forced zero; do not generalize to enormous inputs. Callers hash only width*height cell bytes, never header. NULL digest exits; NULL cells yields sixteen zero bytes, even for length0 (not standard MD5(empty)). Saved-file hashes verified with hashlib; helper/internal compression is not firmware-executed.
